headline_marked: [[E-ink frame]] detects birds by sound, draws them as 1800s illustrations
headline: E-ink frame detects birds by sound, draws them as 1800s illustrations
summary: This Raspberry Pi project uses AI to identify birds by their songs and then renders them using vintage public-domain illustrations.
details: A new project combines an e-ink display with AI to create a unique bird-watching experience. The system listens for bird songs using a microphone and a local AI model called BirdNET-Go to identify the species.

Once a bird is detected, the project fetches a corresponding public-domain illustration from the 1800s. These illustrations are then composited onto a textured paper background, with larger birds positioned more centrally.

The project, called Fugleramme, runs on a Raspberry Pi and uses an Inky Impression e-ink panel for display. It redraws the image only when a new bird species is detected, conserving power and creating a dynamic yet subtle display.

The artwork is sourced from Scandinavian, British, and Central European natural history plates. While the core art is not AI-generated, some minor retouching has been done using AI. Coverage for North America and broader Europe is planned.

The system is still in early development, with plans for more features and broader species coverage. The creator is also offering to build these frames for those who prefer not to assemble them themselves.

headline_marked: [[Java 27 Released]] with default G1 garbage collector and quantum-ready TLS
headline: Java 27 Released with default G1 garbage collector and quantum-ready TLS
summary: The latest Java Development Kit is now generally available, featuring a new default garbage collector and enhanced security protocols for production use.
details: JDK 27, the reference implementation for Java 27, has been officially released and is ready for production environments. This update includes nine key Java Enhancement Proposals (JEPs) that introduce significant improvements and new features.

A major highlight is the adoption of the G1 Garbage Collector as the default across all environments, aiming to improve performance and resource management. The release also bolsters security with post-quantum hybrid key exchange for TLS 1.3, preparing systems for future cryptographic threats.

Further enhancements include the third preview of Lazy Constants and PEM Encodings for cryptographic objects, alongside the fifth preview of Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof, and switch statements. Structured Concurrency reaches its seventh preview, and Compact Object Headers are now enabled by default.

Developers can also benefit from the twelfth incubator of the Vector API for high-performance vectorized operations and JFR In-Process Data Redaction for improved Java Flight Recorder security. As with every release, JDK 27 incorporates hundreds of smaller enhancements and thousands of bug fixes.
